analysis: Reviewed the head_text excerpts of desktop-app/package-lock.json (lines 1667-3224) and the patch excerpt. The visible change is a dev-dependency lockfile refresh. Electron goes 44.5.1 to 44.9.1 and vite 8.3.2 to 8.3.5. @oxc-project/types goes 0.152.0 to 0.155.0, and the @rolldown/binding-* packages go 1.2.12 to 1.2.15. Platform-specific musl/glibc binding entries gain `libc` fields in the changed ranges. The visible entries all resolve to registry.npmjs.org with sha512 integrity hashes. No git, http or file URL sources appear, and no lifecycle or install scripts are added. The visible packages are marked dev:true, so they should not ship in the provider runtime. The lockfile belongs to the desktop-app (Electron), which is not the provider-swift runtime, the coordinator-to-provider WebSocket contract (TB-002), the App Attest authorization path (TB-011) or the attestation chain (TB-009). It does not touch the A-001 to A-018 assets or the T-013/T-034 binary-identity controls. Limits: the patch excerpt is truncated, and later changed ranges (about lines 3679-6703, including the electron entry and the vite/rolldown/lightningcss dependency blocks) were not visible in the supplied units. I could not verify integrity values or resolved URLs there. Electron is the packaged desktop runtime, so its upgrade and any Electron fuse or CSP settings are outside this evidence. No concrete security regression is supported by what I saw. The remaining unverified item is the unseen lockfile sections and package.json. Checking that every changed entry keeps the registry.npmjs.org host and integrity hash is a routine supply-chain check.
